_note: Ordered by information, not convenience. If the queue does not finish, what ran is what mattered most. Every arm runs on suite 0.4.0 so the table is comparable on one version.
_backends: A job's `env` is applied to that job's subprocess only, which is what lets one queue hold both backends: the backend is bound at import time in ollama_client, and every job is already its own process. The two backends CANNOT run together -- llama-server holds ~7.6GB of the 8GB card and Ollama needs its own allocation, so whichever loads second falls off the GPU onto the 10-20x offload cliff M0 measured. No lifecycle automation is attempted: the health gate skips any job whose backend is not serving, and the queue is resumable, so the operator runs it twice. With llama-server up, the nemotron jobs run and the qwen jobs skip; bring Ollama up in its place and re-run, and the reverse happens while the finished nemotron jobs report done.
_reruns_2026-09-17: Everything nemotron is a rerun from zero: the 2026-09-15 sweep is void (llama-server died two tasks in and the harness scored 32 untouched workspaces as results). qwen/judge_bypass is a rerun because the arm never executed at all -- a rotated argument list crashed 90 of its 102 rows, fixed the same day in judge_bypass_workflow.py.

jobs.label: nemotron-baseline
jobs.why: free, no model calls. Identical by construction to the qwen baseline, which makes it the harness sanity check: if these two disagree the backend switch changed something it should not have

jobs.label: nemotron-monolith
jobs.why: one model call, no scaffolding. The cheapest arm that exercises the whole path, so it fails fastest if the backend is wrong -- and the only clean read on what this model does unaided

jobs.label: nemotron-test_synth
jobs.why: the only arm that changes mechanism rather than framing: the model writes an executable witness instead of reading a diff, so its verdict depends on no reading of the worker's code

jobs.label: nemotron-judge_anchored
jobs.why: half of the pair that lifts the anchor confound

jobs.label: nemotron-dloop
jobs.why: the retry-with-failing-lines arm, and the one whose qwen figures move most between the gated and folded metrics (5th to 15th). Worth knowing whether that is the arm or the model

jobs.label: nemotron-m7
jobs.why: the static workflow this project is actually building. Second-largest gated-to-folded drop on qwen

jobs.label: nemotron-m7f
jobs.why: the m7 variant with the largest qwen sample, so the comparison has the firmest other side

jobs.label: nemotron-judge_fullctx
jobs.why: the arm most likely to feel a context ceiling, and this model's ceiling is characterised (M0 entry 1: the wall sits in (65536, 73728] on this card, and the server is sized 2x16384)

jobs.label: nemotron-staged
jobs.why: decomposed pipeline, the other end of the scaffolding range from monolith

jobs.label: nemotron-judge_bypass
jobs.why: first execution of this arm on any model -- the rotated-argument crash meant it had never run. No prior figures exist for it that are worth anything

jobs.label: nemotron-judge_staged
jobs.why: completes the judge family for this model

jobs.label: nemotron-judge_caveat
jobs.why: completes the judge family for this model

jobs.label: nemotron-test_synth_retry
jobs.why: last, because it is the most expensive and the least discriminating of the synth pair

jobs.label: qwen-judge_bypass
jobs.why: REQUIRES OLLAMA, not llama-server -- it will skip until Ollama is the live backend. The arm's 102 recorded rows were 90 crashes and were discarded on 2026-09-17; reps=3 matches the rest of the judge family so the comparison holds on one sample size
